clue.text: Picture of the French copy put beside English

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' (plural)
a crib is a copy, as of another pupil's work

explanation.surface: A copy of a French picture is hung next to an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put beside' simply sets the pieces side by side in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in words is to depict or portray it.

clue.text: Worker taking a cut?

parts.note: looks like someone pocketing a share; to dock is to cut, and the worker is on the docks

explanation.definitionFit: A dock labourer, who loads and unloads ships; docking also means cutting.

clue.text: Some folks can't yet admit being short

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people cannot yet confess to a shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks out the run in folkS CAN'T Yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre, admitting only a small amount; insufficient.

clue.text: Let 26 characters off

indicators.note: the characters are off, out of place, so rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, meaning offer

explanation.surface: A landlord leases out a property with every letter of the alphabet missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TENDER, the answer to 26 across; 'characters' refers to its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to lease it out for payment.

clue.text: Blow the check-out!

parts.note: seems a curse at a shop till; really the roadside test where a driver blows into a device

explanation.definitionFit: A roadside test of a driver's alcohol level, done by blowing into a device.

clue.text: Outlines the changeover in phases

indicators.note: a changeover of the letters of phases means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diagram outlines the switch between project phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlines and forms are both the contours of things, so the verb sense works too: to form or outline.

clue.text: Employ well-qualified person in unpaid situation as a medico

indicators.note: the employment and the graduate go inside the unpaid position

parts.note: HON is short for honorary, an unpaid post
to use is to employ
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Taking on a graduate in an honorary post to work as a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain.

clue.text: Lamentable way to call for backing

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: the summons word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as a witness

explanation.surface: A pathetic route to ask for support.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means pitiful or woeful.

clue.text: Make a song about spring inflation!

indicators.note: the singing goes around the spring

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Fuss loudly over springtime price rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling is a bulge, a puffing up or enlargement.

clue.text: A woman put inside showed distress and cracked

indicators.note: the woman is placed within the word for showing distress

parts.note: cried means wept, showing distress
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman locked in somewhere wept and finally broke down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' looks like a breakdown, but is the definition: full of cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Crannied means full of chinks or fissures, i.e. split with crevices.

clue.text: Sound axiom for retaining a good man

indicators.note: the axiom holds the good man inside it

parts.note: a rule is an axiom or principle
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A maxim upholding the virtue of a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling noise, as of leaves.

clue.text: Having eaten, try making an appeal

indicators.note: the letters are used for making something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: After dinner, someone tries to make a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea.

clue.text: It's true about the record reverse

indicators.note: the word for true goes around the record

parts.note: real means true or genuine
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: It's a fact about the record being flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' hints at a reversal, but is the definition, a verb meaning to undo a law.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or undo it.

clue.text: Muffing gears, gives go-ahead

indicators.note: to muff is to bungle, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver crunching the gears lets the car lurch forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-ahead means pushy and forceful, an assertive, pushing manner.

clue.text: Still state this is deer country

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Unchanging Scotland is described as deer country.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a condition of no movement or development.

clue.text: Thought heel an individual of high aims

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship heels or lists when it leans over

explanation.surface: A notion that someone of lofty purpose is a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like a cad or part of a foot, but is the verb for a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guided by principles and lofty goals over practicality.

clue.text: A criminal who'll take chumps in

parts.note: two chumps, two asses, ass twice

explanation.surface: A con man who preys on fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, a killer for hire.

clue.text: Dog heartless people with neat quarters

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of people are dropped, leaving the first and last

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, as is kine
S and E are compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted crowd with tidy accommodation for their pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but is an old word for cattle, KINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Chinese toy breed with a flat face and long coat.

clue.text: People trained to work on prescribed lines

definitions.text: People trained to work on prescribed lines

parts.words: People trained to work on prescribed lines
parts.note: seems to describe rule-bound workers; prescribed lines are really items on a doctor's prescription, which chemists make up

explanation.definitionFit: Dispensers are pharmacists who make up prescribed medicines.

clue.text: Appear dissatisfied about an evergreen

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pine is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: Looking discontented regarding a fir tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or be discontented.

clue.text: Name given to a town in Belgium, in France, and in Antrim

definitions.text: Name given to a town in Belgium

indicators.note: the second in, with France as a passing aside, says the name sits within the closing words

explanation.surface: A place name shared by towns in several countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nods to Dinan in France; the letters themselves lie in anD IN ANTrim.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinant is a town on the river Meuse in southern Belgium.

clue.text: Fish a small river, being a sportsman

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish
R is an abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler casts on a little stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman who glides on ice.

clue.text: The musician's slow

parts.note: reads as a jibe at a sluggish player, but is the musical direction for a slow tempo

explanation.definitionFit: In music, the Italian tempo marking for a slow pace.

clue.text: 21 is seen as a literary star

indicators.note: the letters are seen recast as something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: the answer to 21 down, a sportsman on ice

explanation.surface: An ice-dancer is hailed as a celebrated writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as' rearranges SKATER (21 down) with IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed star symbol used in text to mark a footnote.

clue.text: How marching men proceed-on foot

definitions.meaning: soldiers on parade keep pace together
part of the foot, the arched upper side

explanation.definitionFit: Marching men keep pace together; it is also the arched top of the foot.

clue.text: Set new limit and a conservationist group will be 13

indicators.note: the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A heritage body fixes a fresh cap and turns combative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set new' rearranges LIMIT. 13 down is AGGRESSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant and combative are synonyms for confrontational behaviour.

clue.text: Offer to be treated with a certain circumspection

definitions.meaning: a formal bid, as in a contract

definitions.text: to be treated with a certain circumspection
definitions.meaning: sore or delicate, needing gentle handling

explanation.definitionFit: A bid formally submitted; also sensitive and delicate, needing care.

clue.text: A salesman-one feeding a duplicator

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
an eater is one who feeds

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman snacks beside the office copier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that repeats, reproducing a thing again, as a copying device does.
